newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index lower at noon on risk control.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index lower at noon on risk control.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index eased lower at noon on Wednesday after China's top securities watchdog called for strengthened risk control in 1997, analysts said.
The foreign currency B index lost 1.62 points or 0.91 percent to 175.47 on turnover of HK$74.3 million.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission has ordered local securities authorities to make risk control their key task for 1997 and work out concrete measures, official media said on Thursday.
"The risk control report made investors slightly nervous, but the mood was not significantly affected because this is an old topic," an analyst at J&A Securities said.

The announcement follows a strong bull run on China's stock markets. Share prices on the Shenzhen and Shanghai stock exchanges have risen more than 50 percent since the start of 1997 despite official warnings on risk, analysts said.
"Investors are particularly sensitive after the index's recent sharp gains," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
The Shenzhen B index achieved 1997 highs for three straight sessions by Monday's close, but began a technical correction on Tuesday.
Analysts said they expected the index to hover in a narrow range for the next few sessions.
"The index should pick up next week unless the government comes out with solid measures to back up today's announcement," the J&A analyst said.
Washing machine maker Little Swan was the biggest loser today, dropping HK$0.58 or 4.40 percent to HK$12.60 on volume of 295,400 shares.
The A shares, which were also hit by the announcement on risk control, fell 3.56 points or 0.75 percent to 474.24 on turnover of 6.68 billion yuan.
Gansu Chengfeng was the worst performer on the A share market, losing 0.34 yuan or 4.80 percent to 6.75 yuan after the appliance maker issued poor 1996 results.
